review_type: Fresh assistant-context source/security review; NOT an independent third-party financial audit
summary: Production readiness is blocked by unverified-email membership pre-hijacking, missing frontend anti-framing policy, and stale successful evidence on early runner failures.

security_concerns.title: Email-based membership grants trust an unverified, attacker-preclaimed address
security_concerns.explanation: In the supported production EMAIL_MODE=delivery configuration, registration creates an active user and establishes a password session without requiring email verification. Adding a colleague by email selects any active account, not a verified email owner. An attacker who pre-registers the intended colleague email receives the owner-authorized membership and can immediately use its role through requireWorkerOrg. REQUIRE_VERIFIED_EMAIL=true guards organization creation only, not membership acquisition or organization access. This is tenant access by email pre-hijacking, not a blockchain-signature bypass.
reproduction: Use an isolated D1 and production bindings with a local MAILER stub returning 200; no mail or external write is required.
SIWE-login an owner and create an organization. Register a second password account using the intended colleague email, but never consume its verification token.
As owner POST /api/orgs/:orgId/members with that email and role=admin. Use the unverified registration session to GET the organization and POST a product.

verifiable_proof.runtime: local real workerd and D1, full production middleware and sessions
verifiable_proof.probe_test: production email preclaim grants unverified password holder invited admin access
verifiable_proof.network: MAILER is an in-process stub; signatures generated in memory; no remote requests

security_concerns.required_fix: Require verified ownership before resolving an email into a membership, and ensure pre-existing unverified email memberships cannot exercise tenant authority. Preserve wallet-only onboarding. Add production delivery-mode regression coverage with an attacker-controlled unverified password session.

security_concerns.title: Production HTML bypasses the API-only anti-framing policy
security_concerns.explanation: The public entry returns ASSETS.fetch unchanged for frontend pages. API middleware sets frame-ancestors none, but that policy protects JSON responses, not the HTML document containing wallet, login, checkout and administrative UI. Neither public nor dist has a _headers file, the production generator supplies no frontend response-header policy, and index.html has no equivalent protection. Production HTML therefore has no application-controlled anti-framing control; API CSRF checks do not stop UI redressing because clicks cause the framed application itself to send valid same-origin requests. Browser third-party-cookie restrictions may limit some cross-site sessions but do not protect wallet/capability UI or same-site hostile origins. No fund-stealing exploit is claimed.
reproduction: Inspect public and dist for _headers: neither exists.

Call the actual public entry fetch for a checkout HTML path with an isolated ASSETS binding returning text/html. Observe it returns the asset unchanged with neither Content-Security-Policy nor X-Frame-Options.
Confirm generated asset routing serves non-API paths directly; thus API response headers cannot supply the HTML framing policy.

verifiable_proof.runtime: local workerd entry-point probe with fixture ASSETS binding
verifiable_proof.probe_test: static HTML asset delegation has no frontend anti-framing headers
verifiable_proof.limitation: Not a deployed-CDN capture or browser exploit; verifies missing application/configuration policy in the reviewed production package.

security_concerns.required_fix: Set an explicit production HTML frame-ancestors policy (normally none; use a narrowly approved allowlist only if embedding is a real requirement) through Static Assets _headers or a correctly routed Worker response. Test actual packaged HTML headers, not only API responses; do not copy the API default-src none onto the SPA.

logic_errors.title: Early verification failures leave a previous passing final report intact
logic_errors.explanation: The new absent-cold-proof guard correctly changes passed to false after a successful child run. However, if a previous final-checks.json has passed=true and the ops subprocess fails, main returns its nonzero status without invalidating that report. Equivalent stale success can survive timeout/exception paths and early child failure. An evidence reader can therefore see a passing final artifact after the current verification failed. This contradicts fail-closed current-source evidence even though the CLI exit code is correctly nonzero.
reproduction: Load scripts/check-phase5-local.py with importlib. Patch ROOT/OUT/BASELINE to a scratch tree. Seed OUT/final-checks.json with {"passed":true,"checks":[]}.
Patch subprocess.run to return CompletedProcess([],1,stdout="isolated intentional ops failure",stderr=""). Invoke main and read the exact scratch final-checks.json.

verifiable_proof.source_review: The cold-proof and frontend guards were also reviewed and their nine current ops unit tests pass; they do not cover this earlier failure path.

logic_errors.required_fix: Invalidate/replace the current report at run start and write a failed verdict on every unsuccessful exit or exception, preserving prior success separately if historical evidence is needed. Add fixtures for preexisting passed=true plus ops failure, child failure, timeout and malformed/missing child report.

verification.note: Real Chrome: delayed chunks, failed chunk recovery/home navigation, deferred wallet provider and real ConnectKit modal. Uses existing dist; no fresh build performed in this read-only review and no claim of fresh build/source identity.

positive_observations: Production config validation enforces secret shape, canonical HTTPS origins, SIWE/domain/chain agreement, secure cookie policy, bounded session lifetimes and explicit email modes; entropy is not falsely certified.
Production API-key creation intentionally returns 503 because key authentication is unimplemented; API keys do not bypass session/RBAC. Lists omit hashes/secrets and grants are admin-only.

API CSRF requires an allowlisted Origin plus exact custom header; JSON media type checks reject JSONP/substrings; body streaming is bounded. Success/error API responses carry no-store, nosniff, no-referrer, restrictive CSP and production HSTS.
Session tokens and API-key records are HMAC protected; production cookies use __Host prefix, HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax. SIWE challenges are purpose/user/message-bound and atomically consumed.

Production configuration generation declares required secret names without serializing values, separates public/private D1 and Worker bindings, disables private public routing/preview and never asserts account ownership or deployment authorization.
Lazy WalletRoutes uses module-scoped Wagmi config and a stable layout; shared QueryClient remains above the layout. Reload/home recovery is available after lazy import failure.

The opt-in official RPC transport probe source uses only four read methods, bundles the actual Rpc into workerd, disposes Miniflare in finally and does not deploy. Existing workerd-official-rpc.json records all four succeeding; reviewer inspected but did not rerun its network probe.

kdf_and_free_tier_assessment.metric: elapsed wall milliseconds, NOT provider CPU
kdf_and_free_tier_assessment.assessment: KDF strength is unchanged. Neither native PBKDF2 await wall time nor full SIWE wall time proves provider billed CPU compliance or incompatibility. Actual production Free-tier CPU/traffic profiling remains a launch gate; do not weaken the KDF or claim successful local tests satisfy it.
